items.parse_summary: A direct how-question asks for Uzziah’s action against Yahweh. The choices are parallel action phrases with Uzziah as the understood actor; none introduces an embedded clause.
A direct question asks how Zebul characterized the figures Gaal saw. The definite phrase “the men” refers back to those figures in the passage.

features.required_operations: Connect this definite noun phrase to the figures Gaal saw and Zebul described as mountain shadows.
features.reason: Identifying the referent is directly relevant to the requested characterization and requires only a short contextual link.

items.parse_summary: A simple object question asks what Micah stole. It contains one named actor and no embedded clauses or modifiers.
A direct why-question asks for the cause of Micah’s anger. The question contains no embedded report, modifier, or additional participant relationship.

The question asks when Zebul becomes angry. The first choice is a hearing-event phrase containing Gaal’s words and their topic, Abimelech; the remaining substantive choices are simple temporal clauses.

features.required_operations: Supply Zebul as the person hearing, distinguish Gaal as the speaker, and identify Abimelech as the topic of the words.
features.reason: These three roles express the triggering event targeted by the item, without additional embedding.

items.parse_summary: The why-question contains a belief clause: Micah thinks that Yahweh will be good to him. The respondent must give Micah’s reason for that belief, with “him” referring to Micah.

features.quote: Why did Micah think Yahweh would be good to him?
features.required_operations: Distinguish Micah’s belief from an independently asserted outcome and retrieve the reason he gives for holding it.
features.reason: The belief layer is necessary to the intended target and is expressed in a single short complement clause.

features.quote: Micah think Yahweh would be good to him
features.required_operations: Resolve “him” to Micah rather than to the embedded subject, Yahweh.
features.reason: The pronoun connects the beneficiary to the believer through one short clause.

items.parse_summary: A direct how-question asks for Abimelech’s method of killing the leaders of Shechem. The substantive choices are short action phrases with Abimelech as the understood actor.

features.required_operations: Resolve “their” to the leaders of Shechem named in the question.
features.reason: This is a local question-to-option reference with no competing plural referent in the item wording.

items.parse_summary: A direct how-question asks for the route by which information reached Paul. “The plan” refers to the plot against him described in the passage.

features.required_operations: Connect the definite phrase to the plot to kill Paul, rather than to his later instruction to the centurion.
features.reason: The reference identifies the information whose transmission is the intended target.

items.parse_summary: A simple identity question asks for the person occupying the father relationship to Abimelech. The choices are individual names plus the standard uncertainty response.
The question embeds the Arameans’ departure within the king’s thinking and asks for the motive he attributes to them. The choices are parallel purpose phrases; “their camp” belongs to the Arameans.

features.quote: Why does the king think the Arameans left their camp?
features.required_operations: Keep the king’s interpretation separate from the actual reason for the departure and select the purpose he attributes to the Arameans.
features.reason: The viewpoint distinction is the intended target, and the purpose-form choices support that reading.

features.required_operations: Resolve “their” to the Arameans within the embedded clause.
features.reason: The possessive has a nearby, explicit antecedent and introduces no extended reference chain.
